name: Li Zhenjiang
current_role: Founder, Chairman and President, China Shineway Pharmaceutical Group (HKEX: 2877)
profile: Li Zhenjiang (b. c.1955) co-founded China Shineway Pharmaceutical, a Hebei-based maker of modern traditional Chinese medicine (injections, soft capsules, granules) listed in Hong Kong since 2004. He joined its predecessor in 1974, has led it since 1984, and still runs overall management and R&D.
interesting_fact: He served as a deputy to China's 10th, 11th and 12th National People's Congress and is vice-chairman of the PRC Chinese Medicine Association.
deep_cut_fact: He joined the factory that became Shineway in 1974, became its head in 1984, and was named an Outstanding Entrepreneur of the PRC Pharmaceutical Industry in 1994; he also holds a National May 1st (Wu Yi) Labour Award.
notes: Low media profile; no published email found in the annual report. Best route is via the company's HK office / company secretary listed on shineway.com.hk.

name: Zhang Xuanning
current_role: Director (non-independent), Yonghui Superstores (SSE: 601933); former vice chairman
profile: Zhang Xuanning co-founded Fuzhou-based fresh-food supermarket chain Yonghui Superstores with his brother Zhang Xuansong, growing it into one of China's largest grocery retailers. He was long its vice chairman; in 2017-18 the brothers sold a 5% stake to Tencent. He was re-elected a director in the March 2025 board overhaul after Miniso's Ye Guofu took a major stake.
interesting_fact: Yonghui pioneered Fuzhou's 'farmers' market to supermarket' (nong gai chao) model in 2001, the fresh-produce focus that drove its national expansion; in 2018 Tencent bought 5% of Yonghui from the brothers for about $648.6m.
deep_cut_fact: When Yonghui Supermarket Co. was registered in 2001, Zhang Xuanning put in RMB 400,000 of the RMB 1 million starting capital, alongside RMB 600,000 from his brother Zhang Xuansong.
notes: Very low public profile; the brothers ended their acting-in-concert agreement in 2018 over strategy differences (avoid in outreach). Route via Yonghui board office email.

name: You Zhenhua
profile: Listed on the 2025 Hurun China Rich List with an estimated RMB ~6.5bn (USD ~910m) fortune attributed to 'Deep Source' (non-ferrous metals processing). Web searches in Chinese and English could not identify the underlying company or confirm this person's role.
notes: Could not identify the company behind 'Deep Source' (深源?) or find any public record of 游振华 as its controller; check the Hurun 2025 list entry directly for the Chinese company name before outreach.

name: Zhang Xingmin
current_role: Co-founding family shareholder (via Chongqing Xiaokang Holdings) of Seres Group (SSE: 601127), formerly Chongqing Xiaokang
profile: The Chinese name 张兴礼 (Zhang Xingli; input romanisation 'Zhang Xingmin' appears off) matches a brother of Seres founder Zhang Xinghai. Xiaokang started in 1986 as a Chongqing seat-spring workshop, then moved into minivans and EVs; renamed Seres in 2022, it builds AITO cars with Huawei. Zhang Xingli is a holder in the controlling company, not a public executive.
interesting_fact: Seres, the Zhang brothers' former motorcycle-parts and minivan business, co-develops the AITO/Wenjie premium EV brand with Huawei. That partnership turned it into one of China's most valuable carmakers.
deep_cut_fact: The family business began in 1986 when Zhang Xinghai put RMB 8,000 into the Baxian Fenghuang Electrical Spring Factory, which made seat springs for Chang'an microvans.
notes: Name mismatch: input says Zhang Xingmin but Chinese is 张兴礼 (Zhang Xingli). Seres' 2023 annual report names 张兴海, 张兴明 and 张兴礼 as loan guarantors; 张兴海 is sole actual controller. Very low profile. The deep-cut fact concerns the family firm's founding by his brother.

name: Wu Zhen
current_role: Founder and co-controlling shareholder, Shanghai i2Finance Software (艾融软件, BSE: 920799); chairwoman from 2014 per its 2019 prospectus
profile: Wu Zhen (b. 1977), an accounting graduate of South-Central Minzu University, spent a decade in IT sales before founding Shanghai i2Finance in 2009. The company builds digital-banking software and services for Chinese financial institutions. She and co-founder Zhang Yan, now chairman, jointly control it; it listed on the Beijing Stock Exchange.
interesting_fact: i2Finance was in the first batch of companies on China's new Beijing Stock Exchange when it opened on 15 Nov 2021. It moved across from the NEEQ 'select tier', which it had joined in 2020.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding i2Finance, she was a sales manager at Shenzhen Aozun Computer (2000-03), an account manager at Computer Associates China (2003-04) and sales director at Yuxin Yicheng, now Yusys (2004-09). She registered i2Finance in 2009 as its sole shareholder.
notes: Fortune shared with co-founder Zhang Yan, who now fronts the company as chairman and GM. Wu Zhen's current board title is unverified. Very low media profile.

name: Bobby Sheng
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Bora Group; CEO, Bora Pharmaceuticals (TWSE: 6472)
profile: Bobby Sheng (b. 1972), a Taiwanese-American raised in California, left UC Berkeley economics at 22 to help run his father's Hoan Pharmaceuticals in Taiwan. He founded Bora in 2007 and grew it through about a dozen acquisitions of plants from Eisai, GSK, Impax/Amneal, Pfizer and others into Taiwan's largest drugmaker and a global CDMO.
interesting_fact: Bora's first factory was a Tainan plant bought from Japan's Eisai in 2013. It went on to buy sites from GSK (Canada), Impax/Amneal (Zhunan) and others, leading Taiwanese media to call Sheng's goal becoming 'the TSMC of pharma'.
deep_cut_fact: Before Bora, Sheng co-founded Machi Entertainment, a digital-first Asian record label, with Taiwanese entertainer Jeff Huang and Korean producer Jay Chong. He also gives new recruits and investors copies of 'Who Moved My Cheese?' to encourage adapting to change.
notes: Based in Taiwan though listed under China by Hurun. Fluent English speaker, US-educated and gives keynotes (e.g. JPM Healthcare Conference 2024), so a strong podcast candidate. Machi Entertainment detail is from Wikipedia citing China Times (chinatimes.com/newspapers/20180307000250-260202).

name: Huang Qingping
current_role: Chairman and Non-executive Director, Yincheng International Holding Co., Ltd. (HKEX: 1902)
profile: Huang Qingping (b. 1963) is the founder and controlling shareholder of Nanjing-based property group Yincheng (银城). Its residential developer Yincheng International listed in Hong Kong in 2019, and he remains non-executive chairman. Yincheng's businesses also include property management (Yincheng Life Service).
interesting_fact: He holds the chairmanship of Yincheng International as a non-executive director; the executive directors running the business include Ma Baohua, Zhu Li, Wang Zheng and Shao Lei (2022 board list).
notes: Very low profile. No published direct contact found; route via Yincheng International's company secretary or IR (see HKEX filings for stock 1902). Research was cut short when the web-search budget ran out.

name: Liao Zhenan
current_role: Actual controller of Shanghai Hanbell Precise Machinery (SZSE: 002158) via Taiwan's Hanbell Investment Holding; chairman 1994-2011, director 2011-2020
profile: Liao Zhenan (廖哲男, Liao Che-nan), from Taiwan, founded the mainland arm of Hanbell, a maker of screw compressors for refrigeration, air conditioning, heat pumps and industrial vacuum pumps. He chaired Shanghai Hanbell from 1994 to 2011 and sat on its board until 2020. He still ultimately controls it through Hanbell Investment Holding (Taiwan), which holds 23.12%.
interesting_fact: Hanbell's 2025 annual report calls it a core equipment supplier for liquid cooling in Chinese AI data centres (AIDC). It leads domestic production of oil-free magnetic-levitation centrifugal compressors (RTM series), a direct tie to an energy and data-centre podcast.
deep_cut_fact: He chaired Shanghai Hanbell for 17 years (1994-2011), then served as a director until 2020; he controls it through a chain running from Hanbell Investment Holding (Taiwan) via BVI and Panamanian holding companies.
notes: Taiwanese national, listed under China by Hurun. No longer on the Shanghai Hanbell board; the Taiwan parent (Hanbell Precise Machinery, Taoyuan) may be a better route. Romanised name may appear as Liao Che-Nan.

name: Lu Boqiang
current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Shenzhen Noposion Crop Science (SZSE: 002215)
profile: Lu Boqiang (卢柏强, b. 1962), a senior agronomist with a master's degree, founded Noposion, one of China's largest pesticide-formulation and crop-protection companies. It has also expanded into specialty-crop (e.g. lychee, citrus) farming services. He directly owns about 24% of the company and chairs it.
interesting_fact: He is vice-president of the China Crop Protection Industry Association and honorary president of the Guangdong Pesticide Association.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Noposion he was a fruit-tree scientist, serving as deputy director and then director of the Fruit Tree Institute at the Shenzhen Agricultural Science Center. In 2008 he was named a National Model Worker of the petroleum and chemical industry.
notes: Route via the board secretary email published in the annual report.

name: Yan Guilin
current_role: Co-founder and shareholder, Guangdong KinLong Hardware Products (SZSE: 002791); left the board in July 2025 when his term expired
profile: Yan Guilin (闫桂林) co-founded KinLong Hardware in Dongguan with chairman Bai Baokun; the company was set up as a joint-stock firm by 47 founding shareholders including the two of them. KinLong makes and distributes architectural hardware such as window, door and curtain-wall fittings. He served as a director until the July 2025 board election.
interesting_fact: KinLong has moved from window and door hardware to 'one-stop' delivery of building hardware, combining product and solution integration with installation and after-sales service, it says in its 2025 annual report.
notes: Low profile; no personal channels. Company board office email is the only published route.

name: Xia Jifa
current_role: Founder and former controlling shareholder, Jiangsu Changling Hydraulic (SSE: 605389); still holds ~17.6% after a 2025 control transfer
profile: Xia Jifa (夏继发) founded Changling Hydraulic in Jiangyin, Jiangsu, which makes central swivel joints, track tensioners and slewing reducers for excavators and aerial work platforms, plus slewing drives for solar trackers. He and his son Xia Zemin, now chairman and GM, controlled the SSE-listed company until a 2025 sale of about 30%.
interesting_fact: In 2025 the Xias sold ~30% of Changling and handed control to Wuxi Hexin Tingtao, a partnership whose concert parties include a Jiangyin high-tech-zone state-asset vehicle. The company's products also include slewing drives for solar trackers.
notes: No longer the controlling shareholder as of Nov 2025. Fortune was shared with his son Xia Zemin, who is the public face of the company.

name: Zhao Chengxia
current_role: Director, Vice President and CFO, Inner Mongolia Yili Industrial Group (SSE: 600887)
profile: Zhao Chengxia (赵成霞) is a long-serving senior executive at Yili, China's largest dairy company, where she is a director, vice president and head of finance. Her wealth comes from a personal stake of about 92.4 million Yili shares, which makes her one of the company's top-ten shareholders, rather than from founding a company.
interesting_fact: A career Yili finance executive, she personally owns about 92 million shares (~1.5%) of the dairy giant, more than many institutional funds on its top-ten shareholder list, and signs Yili's financial statements as head of accounting.
notes: Corporate executive rather than founder; very low personal media profile. qxm@yili.com is the board secretary's published address; info@yili.com is the general company address.

name: Ali Behbahani
current_role: Partner and Co-Head of Healthcare, New Enterprise Associates (NEA)
profile: Ali Behbahani, MD, joined venture firm NEA in 2007 and co-leads its healthcare team, investing in biopharma and medical devices. He sits on boards including Monte Rosa, Korro Bio, Black Diamond and SpyGlass Pharma. He helped NEA incubate cell-therapy companies Arcellx and Nkarta, and earlier worked at The Medicines Company, Morgan Stanley and Lehman Brothers.
interesting_fact: He earned an MD from Penn and an MBA from Wharton at the same time, after Duke bachelor's degrees in biomedical engineering, electrical engineering and chemistry. He says that without venture capital he would have been a surgeon.
deep_cut_fact: His first job was at a McDonald's inside a Walmart in Gainesville, Florida, where he says he learned that 'showing up is half the battle'.
notes: The SEC 'insider holdings' net worth almost certainly reflects NEA fund stakes he reports as a director/10% owner, not personal wealth. Treat as a VC partner, not a UHNW individual. NEA media contact is Erica Sunkin. Biotech-focused, so a weaker fit for an energy/data-centre podcast.

name: Wang Lin
current_role: Founding Partner and Managing Partner, Venture & Growth Capital, CDH Investments (鼎晖投资)
profile: Wang Lin (王霖) co-founded CDH Investments in 2002, when it spun out of CICC's direct-investment arm, and built it into one of China's largest private-equity and alternative-asset managers. He leads CDH's venture and growth-capital business. His fortune comes from carried interest and stakes in CDH funds and the firm.
interesting_fact: CDH grew out of CICC's private-equity group, where Wang was a senior associate from 1999 before co-founding the independent firm in 2002.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a PhD in economics from the Ministry of Finance's Research Institute for Fiscal Sciences. His first job, in 1993-94, was project manager at De Bao Real Estate, a property developer wholly owned by China's Ministry of Finance.
notes: LinkedIn is the firm's page, not his. Ambiguous name, but Hurun's 'CDH' attribution matches the CDH founding partner. Media-shy; go via CDH PR team.

name: Tao Hongxia
current_role: Co-owner of Chongqing Jinke Investment Holding (Group), historical controlling shareholder of Jinke Property Group (SZSE: 000656)
profile: Tao Hongxia (陶虹遐) and Huang Hongyun co-own Chongqing Jinke Investment, which controlled Chongqing-based developer Jinke Property after a 2009-2011 reverse merger into the listed Chongqing Dongyuan. Her wealth came from that stake. Jinke later went through court-supervised restructuring, and its annual report now says it has no actual controller.
interesting_fact: Jinke Property entered the stock market through a 2009-2011 reverse merger into the listed Chongqing Dongyuan Industrial Development, with Jinke Investment as controlling shareholder.
notes: Not a public-facing executive; profile is tied to a co-owner and to Jinke's debt restructuring, so outreach is sensitive and likely unsuitable. Hurun data ends 2021, so current wealth is probably far lower. Alive status not confirmed by a recent source.
